body: On November 18, 2012, Nintendo launches Wii U in North America, before its European arrival on November 30 and Japanese debut on December 8. It is Nintendo's first home console capable of HD output, but its most distinctive idea is not only about resolution. The Wii U GamePad places a 6.2-inch touchscreen directly in the controller and allows information, actions and viewpoints to be distributed between the television and a personal screen. Nintendo speaks of asymmetric play: people in the same room can receive different roles and knowledge. The machine also integrates Miiverse, Nintendo Network, backward compatibility with much of Wii software and hardware, and a more central eShop. Wii U would have a difficult commercial life, but many of its ideas anticipate questions Nintendo would later revisit in a different way with Switch.

The Wii U GamePad combines a touchscreen, sticks, traditional buttons, motion sensors, camera, microphone and remote-control functions in a single object. The most important consequence is that the controller can receive information different from what appears on the television. A map can remain in the player's hands, an inventory can be manipulated without covering the action, or some games can move entirely to the GamePad when the TV is occupied. This flexibility changes the relationship between body and screen: attention is no longer always directed straight ahead, but alternates between shared and private views. The project pays for this ambition with a large controller and distance limits from the console, but it opens a field of experimentation rarely explored by home systems of the period. The second screen is not an accessory; it is the center of the hardware identity.

Nintendo Land is designed as a demonstration of the differences introduced by the GamePad. In some attractions, the player with the personal screen has information that the others, watching the television and using Wii Remotes, cannot see. This asymmetry enables chases, cooperation and competition without asking everyone to perform the same task. It is an important idea because it turns the second screen from an additional panel into a generator of roles. The design must also remain socially understandable: the person holding the GamePad must know what is hidden, while the others must infer how to react without directly controlling that perspective. Nintendo thus tries to renew local multiplayer after Wii's success, not merely by increasing the number of gestures but by distributing information and responsibility differently among the people in the room.

Miiverse attempts to make social interaction a native console function. From the main screen, players see software-related communities, messages, stylus drawings and discussions that can begin directly from a moment of play. The idea differs from a simple friends list: other people's activity becomes a visible surface even while browsing the Wii U ecosystem. Some titles integrate contextual messages into the world, displaying hints, comments or reactions produced by the community. This creates a form of asynchronous presence: people do not need to be online at the same moment to perceive one another. Miiverse would close in 2017, but it remains one of the generation's most recognizable experiments. It shows how Nintendo tried to connect Mii identity, network and software without simply imitating social models already dominant on PC and smartphones.

Wii U is also born from an attempt to retain the enormous audience built by Wii. Nintendo keeps compatibility with Wii discs and most peripherals, including Wii Remotes and Nunchuks, and allows many previously purchased digital contents to be transferred. This choice has both practical and design value. On one hand it lowers the cost of entry for people who already own controllers; on the other it lets multiplayer games use the GamePad and previous-generation devices at the same time. Continuity, however, also contributes to complicated commercial communication: the name and resemblance to Wii make it less immediately obvious that this is a new console. That tension between inheritance and discontinuity helps frame Wii U as a transitional product, rich in ideas but difficult to explain through a single promise.

new_entry.title: Far Cry 3
new_entry.subtitle: Survival and Vaas on the Rook Islands
new_entry.summary: Far Cry 3 is a 2012 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.
body: Far Cry 3 is a 2012 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the third main installment in the Far Cry series after Far Cry 2. The game takes place on the fictional Rook Islands, a tropical archipelago which can be freely explored by players. Gameplay focuses on combat and exploration. Players can use a variety of weapons to defeat human enemies and hostile wildlife, and the game features elements found in role-playing games such as skill trees and experience. After a vacation goes awry, protagonist Jason Brody must save his friends, who have been kidnapped by pirates, and escape from the island and its unhinged inhabitants.

Ubisoft Montreal collaborated with Ubisoft's global development team, including Massive Entertainment, Ubisoft Shanghai, Ubisoft Bucharest, Ubisoft Reflections and Red Storm Entertainment. The game's development was partially restarted in 2010 after the departure of several key creative staff. The team evaluated the feedback for Far Cry 2 and identified areas that needed to be improved or removed. The team spent considerable time designing the island, which they described as the "second most important character" in the game. Inspirations were taken from films and TV shows such as Apocalypse Now and Lost, as well as video games The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Red Dead Redemption. Michael Mando was hired to portray Vaas Montenegro, an antagonist the team compared to Darth Vader. The game was announced in June 2011 and Ubisoft promoted the game with various companion apps, webseries and crossover.

It was released for Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in November 2012. The game received critical acclaim upon release, with praise directed at its characters (particularly Vaas), world design, visuals, progression, and gameplay, though the game's multiplayer modes received criticism. Despite weak pre-order sales, the game was a commercial success, selling 10 million copies. It was nominated for multiple year-end accolades including Game of the Year and Best Shooter awards by several gaming publications. It has also been cited as one of the greatest video games ever made. Ubisoft supported the game with downloadable content and released Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon, the game's standalone expansion, in 2013. A successor, Far Cry 4 was released in November 2014. The game was re-released for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in June 2018 and is set to release for the Nintendo Switch 2 in Spring 2027.

old_entry.title: Far Cry 3
old_entry.summary: Far Cry 3 is a 2012 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.
body: Far Cry 3 is a 2012 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the third main installment in the Far Cry series after Far Cry 2. The game takes place on the fictional Rook Islands, a tropical archipelago which can be freely explored by players. Gameplay focuses on combat and exploration. Players can use a variety of weapons to defeat human enemies and hostile wildlife, and the game features elements found in role-playing games such as skill trees and experience. After a vacation goes awry, protagonist Jason Brody must save his friends, who have been kidnapped by pirates, and escape from the island and its unhinged inhabitants.

Ubisoft Montreal collaborated with Ubisoft's global development team, including Massive Entertainment, Ubisoft Shanghai, Ubisoft Bucharest, Ubisoft Reflections and Red Storm Entertainment. The game's development was partially restarted in 2010 after the departure of several key creative staff. The team evaluated the feedback for Far Cry 2 and identified areas that needed to be improved or removed. The team spent considerable time designing the island, which they described as the "second most important character" in the game. Inspirations were taken from films and TV shows such as Apocalypse Now and Lost, as well as video games The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Red Dead Redemption. Michael Mando was hired to portray Vaas Montenegro, an antagonist the team compared to Darth Vader. The game was announced in June 2011 and Ubisoft promoted the game with various companion apps, webseries and crossover.

It was released for Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in November 2012. The game received critical acclaim upon release, with praise directed at its characters (particularly Vaas), world design, visuals, progression, and gameplay, though the game's multiplayer modes received criticism. Despite weak pre-order sales, the game was a commercial success, selling 10 million copies. It was nominated for multiple year-end accolades including Game of the Year and Best Shooter awards by several gaming publications. It has also been cited as one of the greatest video games ever made. Ubisoft supported the game with downloadable content and released Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon, the game's standalone expansion, in 2013. A successor, Far Cry 4 was released in November 2014. The game was re-released for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in June 2018 and is set to release for the Nintendo Switch 2 in Spring 2027.

new_entry.title: New Super Mario Bros. U
new_entry.subtitle: Mario joins the Wii U launch in high definition
new_entry.summary: Mario reaches high-definition worlds as a Wii U launch title. New Super Mario Bros. U carries forward cooperative platforming while sending the group back to rescue Peach and her castle.
body: New Super Mario Bros. U is a 2012 platform game developed and published by Nintendo as a launch title for the Wii U. A sequel to New Super Mario Bros. Wii and the fourth and final entry in the New Super Mario Bros. series, following New Super Mario Bros. 2, it is the first Super Mario game to feature high-definition graphics. The plot follows Mario on his way to rescue Princess Peach and her castle from Bowser. The game retains the cooperative multiplayer mode from its prior entry.

Development of New Super Mario Bros. U started after the release of New Super Mario Bros. Wii, and the game was revealed at E3 2011. Takashi Tezuka explained that he created the game to take advantage of the Wii U, introducing the Boost mode and Miiverse integration.

The game received generally positive reviews from critics who praised its gameplay, graphics, and additions; but it was criticized for its unoriginality compared to prior titles and for having what some perceived as an uninteresting atmosphere. The game became the third best-selling Wii U game, and received an expansion pack named New Super Luigi U as part of the "Year of Luigi" campaign. A Nintendo Switch port named New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe was released worldwide on January 11, 2019, followed by a release for China on December 10, 2019. As of March 2025, both versions combined have sold over 24 million copies.

old_entry.title: New Super Mario Bros. U
old_entry.summary: Mario reaches high-definition worlds as a Wii U launch title. New Super Mario Bros. U carries forward cooperative platforming while sending the group back to rescue Peach and her castle.
body: New Super Mario Bros. U is a 2012 platform game developed and published by Nintendo as a launch title for the Wii U. A sequel to New Super Mario Bros. Wii and the fourth and final entry in the New Super Mario Bros. series, following New Super Mario Bros. 2, it is the first Super Mario game to feature high-definition graphics. The plot follows Mario on his way to rescue Princess Peach and her castle from Bowser. The game retains the cooperative multiplayer mode from its prior entry.

Development of New Super Mario Bros. U started after the release of New Super Mario Bros. Wii, and the game was revealed at E3 2011. Takashi Tezuka explained that he created the game to take advantage of the Wii U, introducing the Boost mode and Miiverse integration.

The game received generally positive reviews from critics who praised its gameplay, graphics, and additions; but it was criticized for its unoriginality compared to prior titles and for having what some perceived as an uninteresting atmosphere. The game became the third best-selling Wii U game, and received an expansion pack named New Super Luigi U as part of the "Year of Luigi" campaign. A Nintendo Switch port named New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe was released worldwide on January 11, 2019, followed by a release for China on December 10, 2019. As of March 2025, both versions combined have sold over 24 million copies.

new_entry.title: Fantasy Life
new_entry.subtitle: A profession can change the journey
new_entry.summary: On December 27, 2012, LEVEL-5 released Fantasy Life in Japan for Nintendo 3DS, in both physical and digital form.
body: On December 27, 2012, LEVEL-5 released Fantasy Life in Japan for Nintendo 3DS, in both physical and digital form. The game imagines a role not as a permanent class, but as a profession that can be changed during the adventure. Twelve Lives connect combat, gathering and crafting: what is mined as a Miner can become material for a Blacksmith and finally equipment for a combat profession. This circulation turns progression into a small personal economy. Reveria also invites the player to slow down, furnish homes, collect objects and pursue activities that do not always serve the main story. LEVEL-5 entrusts the music to Nobuo Uematsu and the illustrative artwork to Yoshitaka Amano, building a bright, everyday fantasy. Fantasy Life thus proposes an RPG in which changing jobs means changing the way the same world is seen.

Fantasy Life's Life System allows the player to change profession and retain useful skills even when taking on a different role. Nintendo describes twelve Lives organized around combat, gathering and crafting, and explicitly shows how they can support one another: a Miner extracts metals, a Blacksmith turns them into weapons, and a combat profession can then use them in the field. Progression therefore does not belong to a single class. Every profession adds a perspective on the same set of resources and problems. Changing Life does not mean starting from zero, but expanding the circuit of possibilities. This structure makes even an apparently peaceful profession meaningful, because creating better tools changes what can later be gathered or confronted. The character grows as the sum of professional experiences, not as an identity fixed by an irreversible initial choice.

Fantasy Life makes the value of a material readable by showing several stages of its transformation. An ore is not merely an object to sell: through a crafting profession it can become a component, weapon or tool. Nintendo presents the game precisely through this relationship between gathering, creating and fighting. The result is a progression system in which many activities produce consequences beyond their immediate context. Improving as a Carpenter can change the furnishings in a home; advancing as a Blacksmith can make another Life more effective; exploring a new region opens materials that feed both. This network reduces the usual separation between the main quest and side activities. Even a session spent fishing or cutting wood can build future possibilities. The world thus becomes a system of resources to understand, not merely scenery crossed between one battle and the next.

Fantasy Life does not build Reveria only as a land to save. Nintendo emphasizes the ability to buy homes in different towns, decorate them with furniture created by the player and alternate adventure, gathering and everyday activities. This flexibility defines the work's tone. A volcano or dangerous area may matter because it contains rare materials, but the result of that exploration can become a piece of furniture, a tool or a personal item rather than simply a weapon. LEVEL-5 strengthens this domestic fantasy by entrusting the soundtrack to Nobuo Uematsu and the illustrative artwork to Yoshitaka Amano, two creators associated with epic worlds but here placed within a lighter, more modular project. Heroism does not disappear: it shares space with the pleasure of choosing a profession, decorating and changing pace without feeling outside the adventure.

old_entry.summary: On December 27, 2012, LEVEL-5 released Fantasy Life in Japan for Nintendo 3DS, in both physical and digital form.
body: On December 27, 2012, LEVEL-5 released Fantasy Life in Japan for Nintendo 3DS, in both physical and digital form. The game imagines a role not as a permanent class, but as a profession that can be changed during the adventure. Twelve Lives connect combat, gathering and crafting: what is mined as a Miner can become material for a Blacksmith and finally equipment for a combat profession. This circulation turns progression into a small personal economy. Reveria also invites the player to slow down, furnish homes, collect objects and pursue activities that do not always serve the main story. LEVEL-5 entrusts the music to Nobuo Uematsu and the illustrative artwork to Yoshitaka Amano, building a bright, everyday fantasy. Fantasy Life thus proposes an RPG in which changing jobs means changing the way the same world is seen.

Fantasy Life's Life System allows the player to change profession and retain useful skills even when taking on a different role. Nintendo describes twelve Lives organized around combat, gathering and crafting, and explicitly shows how they can support one another: a Miner extracts metals, a Blacksmith turns them into weapons, and a combat profession can then use them in the field. Progression therefore does not belong to a single class. Every profession adds a perspective on the same set of resources and problems. Changing Life does not mean starting from zero, but expanding the circuit of possibilities. This structure makes even an apparently peaceful profession meaningful, because creating better tools changes what can later be gathered or confronted. The character grows as the sum of professional experiences, not as an identity fixed by an irreversible initial choice.

Fantasy Life makes the value of a material readable by showing several stages of its transformation. An ore is not merely an object to sell: through a crafting profession it can become a component, weapon or tool. Nintendo presents the game precisely through this relationship between gathering, creating and fighting. The result is a progression system in which many activities produce consequences beyond their immediate context. Improving as a Carpenter can change the furnishings in a home; advancing as a Blacksmith can make another Life more effective; exploring a new region opens materials that feed both. This network reduces the usual separation between the main quest and side activities. Even a session spent fishing or cutting wood can build future possibilities. The world thus becomes a system of resources to understand, not merely scenery crossed between one battle and the next.

Fantasy Life does not build Reveria only as a land to save. Nintendo emphasizes the ability to buy homes in different towns, decorate them with furniture created by the player and alternate adventure, gathering and everyday activities. This flexibility defines the work's tone. A volcano or dangerous area may matter because it contains rare materials, but the result of that exploration can become a piece of furniture, a tool or a personal item rather than simply a weapon. LEVEL-5 strengthens this domestic fantasy by entrusting the soundtrack to Nobuo Uematsu and the illustrative artwork to Yoshitaka Amano, two creators associated with epic worlds but here placed within a lighter, more modular project. Heroism does not disappear: it shares space with the pleasure of choosing a profession, decorating and changing pace without feeling outside the adventure.

new_entry.title: Tomb Raider
new_entry.subtitle: Lara Croft begins again on Yamatai
new_entry.summary: Tomb Raider is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Crystal Dynamics and published by Square Enix.
body: Tomb Raider is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Crystal Dynamics and published by Square Enix. It is the tenth main entry and a reboot of the Tomb Raider series, acting as the first instalment in the Survivor trilogy that reconstructs the origins of Lara Croft. The game was released for PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360 on 5 March 2013. Gameplay focuses on survival, with exploration when traversing the island and visiting various optional tombs. It is the first game in the main series to have multiplayer and the first game in the series to be published by Square Enix after the latter's acquisition of Eidos Interactive in 2009.

Crystal Dynamics began development of Tomb Raider soon after the release of Tomb Raider: Underworld in 2008. Rather than a sequel, the team decided to reboot the series, re-establishing the origins of Lara Croft for the second time, as they did with Tomb Raider: Legend. Tomb Raider is set on Yamatai, an island from which Lara, who is untested and not yet the battle-hardened explorer she is in other titles in the series, must save her friends and escape while being hunted down by a malevolent cult. Camilla Luddington was hired to voice and perform as Lara Croft, replacing Keeley Hawes.

Tomb Raider received acclaim and is considered by critics to be one of the greatest video games ever made; it received praise for its graphics, gameplay, Luddington's performance as Lara, and Lara's characterization and development, although the addition of a multiplayer mode was criticized. The game sold over 14.5 million units worldwide by October 2021, making it the best-selling Tomb Raider title to date. A remastered version, Tomb Raider: Definitive Edition, featuring improved graphics, new control features, and downloadable content, was released for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in January 2014, for Windows in April 2024, and for Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 in November 2025. An Android and iOS version was released in February 2026. The game was followed by Rise of the Tomb Raider (2015) and Shadow of the Tomb Raider (2018).

new_entry.title: God of War: Ascension
new_entry.subtitle: Kratos breaks his oath to Ares
new_entry.summary: God of War: Ascension is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.
body: God of War: Ascension is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. Released in March 2013, it is the seventh installment in the God of War series and the second chronologically. Loosely based on Greek mythology, it is set in ancient Greece with vengeance as its central motif. The player controls the protagonist, Kratos, the former servant of the God of War Ares, who tricked Kratos into killing his own wife and daughter. In response to this tragedy, Kratos renounced Ares, breaking his blood oath to the god. Kratos was, therefore, imprisoned and tortured by the three Furies, guardians of honor and enforcers of punishment. Helped by the oath keeper, Orkos, Kratos escapes his imprisonment and confronts the Furies, aiming to free himself of his bond to Ares.

The gameplay is similar to previous installments, focusing on combo-based combat with the player's main weapon, the Blades of Chaos, and other weapons acquired by the game's World Weapons mechanic. It continues the use of quick time events from previous entries but also utilizes a promptless free-form system. Four magical attacks and a power-enhancing ability can be used as alternative combat options, and the game features puzzles and platforming elements. The game also features a redesigned combat system, gameplay mechanics not available in previous installments, and downloadable content. Notably, Ascension was the first installment in the series to include multiplayer, which is online-only and features modes for both competitive and cooperative play. From October 2012 to March 2013, a social experience was available online in the form of a graphic novel titled Rise of the Warrior, a prequel story that tied into the game's single-player and multiplayer modes. Ascension was the last game in the series to be based on Greek mythology until the 2026 title, Sons of Sparta; the franchise shifted to Norse mythology with 2018's God of War and its 2022 sequel Ragnarök, with Christopher Judge replacing Terrence C. Carson as the voice of Kratos.

God of War: Ascension received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its fundamental gameplay and spectacle as true to the series, although the story was deemed to be less compelling than in previous installments. The game's multiplayer element received mixed responses: although reviewers found that the gameplay translated well into the multiplayer setting, they criticized the balance and depth of combat. Ascension sold less than its predecessor, with over 3 million units shipped and received no awards, but it did, however, receive several nominations, including "Outstanding Achievement in Videogame Writing" at the Writers Guild of America Videogame Awards and the Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences award for "Outstanding Achievement in Sound Design".

Four magical attacks and a power-enhancing ability can be used as alternative combat options, and the game features puzzles and platforming elements. The game also features a redesigned combat system, gameplay mechanics not available in previous installments, and downloadable content. Notably, Ascension was the first installment in the series to include multiplayer, which is online-only and features modes for both competitive and cooperative play. From October 2012 to March 2013, a social experience was available online in the form of a graphic novel titled Rise of the Warrior, a prequel story that tied into the game's single-player and multiplayer modes. Ascension was the last game in the series to be based on Greek mythology until the 2026 title, Sons of Sparta; the franchise shifted to Norse mythology with 2018's God of War and its 2022 sequel Ragnarök, with Christopher Judge replacing Terrence C. Carson as the voice of Kratos.

God of War: Ascension received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its fundamental gameplay and spectacle as true to the series, although the story was deemed to be less compelling than in previous installments. The game's multiplayer element received mixed responses: although reviewers found that the gameplay translated well into the multiplayer setting, they criticized the balance and depth of combat. Ascension sold less than its predecessor, with over 3 million units shipped and received no awards, but it did, however, receive several nominations, including "Outstanding Achievement in Videogame Writing" at the Writers Guild of America Videogame Awards and the Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences award for "Outstanding Achievement in Sound Design".

new_entry.summary: Kentucky Route Zero is a 2013–2020 point-and-click adventure interactive fiction game developed by Cardboard Computer and published by Annapurna Interactive.
body: Kentucky Route Zero is a 2013–2020 point-and-click adventure interactive fiction game developed by Cardboard Computer and published by Annapurna Interactive. The game follows the narrative of a truck driver named Conway and the strange people he meets as he tries to cross the mysterious Route Zero in Kentucky to make a final delivery for the antiques company he works for.
The game received acclaim for its visual art, narrative, characterization, atmosphere, and themes, appearing on several best-of-the-decade lists.

Kentucky Route Zero was first revealed in 2011 via the crowdfunding platform Kickstarter and is separated into five acts that were released sporadically throughout its development; the first releasing in January 2013 and the last releasing in January 2020. The game was developed for Linux, Windows, and macOS, with console ports for the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One under the subtitle of "TV Edition", coinciding with the release of the final act. The game was released for Android and iOS on December 13, 2022, in partnership with Netflix and was later released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S in August 2023.

new_entry.title: DmC: Devil May Cry
new_entry.subtitle: A Reboot Built to Provoke
new_entry.summary: On January 15, 2013, DmC: Devil May Cry arrives on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in North America and Europe.
body: On January 15, 2013, DmC: Devil May Cry arrives on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in North America and Europe. Capcom gives Ninja Theory an awkward task: reinterpret a series defined as much by combat precision as by the image of its protagonist. The new Dante is placed inside a contemporary, deformable city called Limbo, while combat asks players to switch between Angel and Demon powers in real time. DmC does not try to be unobtrusive. It uses the reboot as friction, questioning tone, silhouette and presentation while attempting to preserve the basic pleasure of chaining weapons, movement and style.

Capcom asks Ninja Theory to treat DmC as a contemporary reinterpretation rather than an aesthetic copy of earlier entries. The most visible change is Dante: younger, placed in an urban environment and built around a different identity. But the design problem is deeper. A Devil May Cry reboot has to feel new without losing the sense of control that makes the series recognizable. The game therefore keeps combos, style ratings, enemy launchers and rapid weapon switching while changing tone and context. The tension between familiarity and rupture is not hidden. DmC places it at the centre and accepts that players will measure every novelty against a very precise memory of how Dante is supposed to move.

The Angel and Demon system gives the triggers the job of changing Dante's behaviour instantly. Holding one modifier opens Angel weapons and abilities, fast and useful for controlling groups; the other brings in heavier, more powerful Demon tools. The choice does not create three separate characters but one continuous flow in which the player moves between categories during the same combo. Traversal also uses this logic, pulling Dante toward targets or dragging elements toward him. Capcom presents the mechanic as something new that must coexist with the series' established foundations. The result tries to make a broad arsenal readable by using the player's fingers as switches, reducing the distance between intention and weapon change.

Limbo does not function as simple scenery. Streets, walls and signs can deform, narrow passages and turn architecture into an hostile force. Ninja Theory uses Unreal Engine 3 and custom work on materials, lighting, particles and cinematic tools, pursuing a highly colourful, stylised image when much contemporary action design favoured muted palettes. This direction lets the level comment on the action: the city watches Dante, insults him through graphic language and changes shape to obstruct him. Technology therefore serves both narrative and spatial choices. DmC wants the world to feel as though it is being edited against the protagonist in real time, like the set of a music video suddenly becoming level design and forcing the player to keep moving.

new_entry.title: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance
new_entry.subtitle: Raiden takes Metal Gear into action combat
new_entry.summary: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance takes Raiden into a direct action game developed by PlatinumGames with Kojima Productions.
body: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance takes Raiden into a direct action game developed by PlatinumGames with Kojima Productions. Released in 2013, it follows the cyborg swordsman in a world where private military companies employ advanced combat technology. The familiar Metal Gear setting now supports a different kind of confrontation.

Blade Mode lets the player aim the direction of Raiden's sword rather than simply watch a fixed finishing animation. A carefully placed strike can expose an enemy's energy source for Zandatsu. Cutting becomes both a visible effect and a way to recover the resources needed to keep fighting.

PlatinumGames records that the project began as Metal Gear Solid: Rising, intended to bridge earlier appearances of Raiden. When the collaboration changed, the setting moved to several years after Metal Gear Solid 4. The finished game therefore reflects a production change in its story as well as in its combat.

new_entry.title: Gears of War: Judgment
new_entry.subtitle: A Military Trial Rewrites the Gears Campaign
new_entry.summary: Gears of War: Judgment revisits the war through Kilo Squad and asks players to change the terms of an encounter.
body: Gears of War: Judgment follows Kilo Squad shortly after Emergence Day, before the events of the original trilogy. Damon Baird and Augustus Cole fight alongside Sofia Hendrick and Garron Paduk in Halvo Bay. Epic Games and People Can Fly released the Xbox 360 game in March 2013.

Its Mission Declassification system introduces additional challenges during the campaign. The Smart Spawn System can vary enemy types, arrival times and positions. A familiar combat space can consequently ask a different question on a return visit, rather than relying entirely on remembering where every opponent appeared before.

OverRun changes the shape of multiplayer through five-player teams with distinct classes. Teams alternate between the COG and Locust, so attacking and defending require different tools and responsibilities. It extends the series' cover-based firefights into a contest where understanding another role is part of understanding the battle.

Development on Gears of War: Judgment began after the release of Gears of War 3 in September 2011. Epic Games brought in developer People Can Fly to lead the development, making this Epic and People Can Fly's second collaboration after Bulletstorm. PCF was previously developing a sequel to Bulletstorm before being assigned to work on Judgment.

old_entry.summary: Gears of War: Judgment revisits the war through Kilo Squad and asks players to change the terms of an encounter.
body: Gears of War: Judgment follows Kilo Squad shortly after Emergence Day, before the events of the original trilogy. Damon Baird and Augustus Cole fight alongside Sofia Hendrick and Garron Paduk in Halvo Bay. Epic Games and People Can Fly released the Xbox 360 game in March 2013.

Its Mission Declassification system introduces additional challenges during the campaign. The Smart Spawn System can vary enemy types, arrival times and positions. A familiar combat space can consequently ask a different question on a return visit, rather than relying entirely on remembering where every opponent appeared before.

OverRun changes the shape of multiplayer through five-player teams with distinct classes. Teams alternate between the COG and Locust, so attacking and defending require different tools and responsibilities. It extends the series' cover-based firefights into a contest where understanding another role is part of understanding the battle.

Development on Gears of War: Judgment began after the release of Gears of War 3 in September 2011. Epic Games brought in developer People Can Fly to lead the development, making this Epic and People Can Fly's second collaboration after Bulletstorm. PCF was previously developing a sequel to Bulletstorm before being assigned to work on Judgment.
